L317@P10: Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements
L318@P10: 1. Organization
L319@P10: Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical Inc., or the Company, is a biopharmaceutical company incorporated in Delaware.
L320@P10: The Company is focused on the identification, acquisition, development, and commercialization of novel products for the treatment of
L321@P10: serious rare and ultra-rare genetic diseases. The Company operates as one reportable segment and has six commercially approved
L322@P10: products.
L323@P10: CRYSVITA® (burosumab) is approved in the United States, or U.S., the European Union, or EU, and certain other regions for the
L324@P10: treatment of X-linked hypophosphatemia, or XLH, in adult and pediatric patients one year of age and older. CRYSVITA is also approved in
L325@P10: the U.S. and certain other regions for the treatment of fibroblast growth factor 23, or FGF23-related hypophosphatemia in tumor-induced
L326@P10: osteomalacia, or TIO, associated with phosphaturic mesenchymal tumors that cannot be curatively resected or localized in adults and
L327@P10: pediatric patients 2 years of age and older.
L328@P10: MEPSEVII® (vestronidase alfa) is approved in the U.S., the EU and certain other regions, as the first medicine for the treatment of
L329@P10: children and adults with mucopolysaccharidosis VII, or MPS VII, also known as Sly syndrome.
L330@P10: DOJOLVI® (triheptanoin) is approved in the U.S. and certain other regions for the treatment of pediatric and adult patients severely
L331@P10: affected by long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders, or LC-FAOD.
L332@P10: EVKEEZA® (evinacumab) is approved in the U.S., the European Economic Area, or EEA, Brazil, Mexico, and Japan for the treatment
L333@P10: of homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, or HoFH. The Company has exclusive rights to commercialize EVKEEZA® (evinacumab)
L334@P10: outside of the U.S.
L335@P10: GENGLYCOS® (pariglasgene brecaparvovec-opnr) is approved in the U.S. for the treatment of pediatric and adult patients eight years
L336@P10: and older with glycogen storage disease type Ia, or GSDIa.
L337@P10: FAYUVI® (rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf) is approved in the U.S. for the treatment of pediatric patients with Sanfilippo syndrome
L338@P10: type A, or MPS IIIA, a rare lysosomal storage disease.
L339@P10: In addition to the approved products, the Company has the following ongoing clinical development programs:
L340@P10: • DTX301 is an AAV8 gene therapy product candidate in development for the treatment of patients with ornithine
L341@P10: transcarbamylase, or OTC deficiency, the most common urea cycle disorder;
L342@P10: • UX016 is a small-molecule prodrug of sialic acid, or SA, being evaluated as a substrate replacement therapy for GNE myopathy;
L343@P10: and
L344@P10: • UX143 which is subject to the Company’s collaboration agreement with Mereo BioPharma 3, or Mereo, is a fully human
L345@P10: monoclonal antibody that inhibits sclerostin, a protein that acts on a key bone-signaling pathway and inhibits the activity of boneforming cells for the treatment of patients with Osteogenesis Imperfecta, or OI.
L346@P10: The Company has sustained operating losses to date, and its ultimate success depends on the outcome of its research and
L347@P10: development and commercialization activities. Through September 30, 2026, the Company has relied primarily on the sale of equity
L348@P10: securities, revenues from commercial products, the sale of certain future royalties, strategic collaboration arrangements, and the sale of U.S.
L349@P10: Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, priority review vouchers, or PRVs, to finance its operations. The Company may need to raise
L350@P10: additional capital to fully implement its business plans through the issuance of equity, borrowings, or strategic alliances with partner
L351@P10: companies. However, if such financing is not available at adequate levels, the Company would need to reevaluate its operating plans.
L352@P10: 2. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
L353@P10: Basis of Presentation
L354@P10: The accompanying unaudited Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements include the accounts of the Company and its whollyowned subsidiaries. The Company consolidates any variable interest entity, or VIE, for which it is the primary beneficiary. Certain
L355@P10: reclassifications have been made to prior periods in the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements and accompanying notes to conform
L356@P10: with the current presentation.
L357@P10: The financial statements have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, or GAAP, for interim
L358@P10: financial information and in accordance with the instructions to Form 10-Q and Rule 10-01 of Regulation S-X. Accordingly, they do not
L359@P10: include all of the information and footnotes required by GAAP for complete financial statements. The unaudited interim Condensed
L360@P10-11: Consolidated Financial Statements have been prepared on the same basis as the annual financial statements. In the10
L361@P11: opinion of management, the accompanying unaudited Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements reflect all adjustments (consisting only
L362@P11: of normal recurring adjustments) considered necessary for a fair presentation. All intercompany accounts and transactions have been
L363@P11: eliminated. These financial statements should be read in conjunction with the audited financial statements and notes thereto for the
L364@P11: preceding fiscal year contained in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K filed on February 18, 2026, or Annual Report, with the United
